latest_release.body:
We're pleased to announce that Dangerzone 0.11.1 has been released.
This release mostly includes stability improvements and security fixes, with a few new features.

The highlights for this release are:

* Users can now choose to disable or skip update checks.  
* GitHub release notes are no longer rendered from Markdown to HTML in the application.  
* Documents are now accepted from stdin, and safe PDFs are written to stdout.  
* (Linux-only) Users now get progress reports for image downloads.  
* Documentation is now published at [https\://docs.dangerzone.rocks](https://docs.dangerzone.rocks).

## Security fixes

An internal security assessment fixed two vulnerabilities in the `dangerzone-image load-archive` command, which is used to update the Dangerzone sandbox on offline (air-gapped) computers. A malicious archive could create or overwrite files on your computer, or be passed to Podman before Dangerzone checked that it came from us ([GHSA-m282-wfqf-935m](https://github.com/freedomofpress/dangerzone/security/advisories/GHSA-m282-wfqf-935m), [GHSA-pfm5-gp85-8g5p](https://github.com/freedomofpress/dangerzone/security/advisories/GHSA-pfm5-gp85-8g5p)).

Converting documents is not affected, and most users are not affected either. If you install sandbox updates with `dangerzone-image load-archive`, you are **strongly** advised to update and to load only those archives that you have prepared yourself. For more details, see our [security advisory](https://docs.dangerzone.rocks/0.11.1/advisories/2026-10-22/).

Also, the Dangerzone project now has a formal [security policy](https://github.com/freedomofpress/dangerzone/security/policy), so if you find other issues like this in our codebase, make sure to check it out.


## Platform changes

* Add support for Fedora 45  
* Add support for Ubuntu 26.10  
* Make Dangerzone work on Tails 7.10.1+

## Community contributions

For this release, we had help from community members. We want to thank:

* @marekl11, who added a mention to Winget as an alternative installation method, and fixed a typo ([#1557](https://github.com/freedomofpress/dangerzone/pull/1557), [#1556](https://github.com/freedomofpress/dangerzone/pull/1556)).  
* @vbrekher, who fixed a long-standing issue in our GUI regarding unreadable documents ([#1558](https://github.com/freedomofpress/dangerzone/pull/1558)).  
* All members who reported issues and opened discussions in our GitHub repo, thanks for helping us improve Dangerzone!

For a full list of the changes, see our [changelog](https://github.com/freedomofpress/dangerzone/blob/v0.11.1/CHANGELOG.md#0111).

detail.readme:
# Dangerzone

Take potentially dangerous PDFs, office documents, or images and convert them to a safe PDF.


| ![Settings](./assets/screenshot1.png) | ![Converting](./assets/screenshot2.png)
|--|--|

Dangerzone works like this: You give it a document that you don't know if you can trust (for example, an email attachment). Inside of a sandbox, Dangerzone converts the document to a PDF (if it isn't already one), and then converts the PDF into raw pixel data: a huge list of RGB color values for each page. Then, outside of the sandbox, Dangerzone takes this pixel data and converts it back into a PDF.

_Read more about Dangerzone in the [official site](https://dangerzone.rocks/about/)._

## Getting started

The documentation lives at [docs.dangerzone.rocks](https://docs.dangerzone.rocks/).
Its source is under [`docs/`](docs/) in this repository:

* [Installation](https://docs.dangerzone.rocks/latest/how-to/install/) for macOS, Windows, Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Qubes OS, and Tails, and the [supported platforms](https://docs.dangerzone.rocks/latest/reference/supported-platforms/)
* [Tutorials](https://docs.dangerzone.rocks/latest/tutorials/convert-your-first-document/) to get started
* [Development environment](https://docs.dangerzone.rocks/latest/tutorials/run-dangerzone-from-source/) to build from source, and [how to contribute](https://docs.dangerzone.rocks/latest/reference/changelog/)
* [Security policy](SECURITY.md) and [changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

Preview the site locally with `poetry install --with docs` followed by `make docs-serve`.
